ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The conveyor belt is inclined at an angle of $\theta = 30^\circ$ to the horizontal and moves clockwise at a speed of $\mathbf{v} = 2 \mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}$. A block slides onto the conveyor belt from the bottom with an initial speed of $\mathbf{v_0} = 6 \mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the conveyor belt is $\upmu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}$. The block fails to reach the top of the conveyor belt and slides back down. The acceleration due to gravity is $\mathrm{g} = 10 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$.

1. Find the minimum length $l_0$ of the conveyor belt.
2. Ignoring the size of the pulley, the length of the conveyor belt is $l_0$. Find the length $s$ of the scratch left by the block on the conveyor belt from the moment the block slides onto the conveyor belt until it leaves.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a conveyor belt inclined from the lower left to the upper right, with a pulley at each of the upper and lower ends; the inclination angle θ is marked at the lower left end, and the block enters the inclined plane from the lower left end and has an arrow of initial velocity v0; an arrow of velocity v is marked on the belt surface, and there is an arrow of rotation direction beside the upper-right pulley. According to the problem statement and the figure, take the direction of the upper inclined belt as the direction of study, and let the x-axis be positive upward along the inclined plane. Reasoning: It is known that θ=30°, the conveyor belt speed v=2 m/s, the block initial velocity v0=6 m/s, μ=√3/5, and g=10 m/s². Along the inclined plane direction, the gravitational component is g sinθ=10×1/2=5 m/s², and the magnitude of the frictional acceleration is μg cosθ=(√3/5)×10×(√3/2)=3 m/s². First stage: The block speed 6 m/s is greater than the conveyor belt speed 2 m/s, and the block slides upward relative to the belt surface, so the kinetic friction force is downward along the inclined plane. The resultant acceleration a1=-(5+3)=-8 m/s². The time for the block to decrease from 6 m/s to 2 m/s is t1=(6-2)/8=0.5 s, and the displacement x1=(6²-2²)/(2×8)=2 m. Second stage: After the block speed is less than the conveyor belt speed, the belt surface moves upward relative to the block, and the friction force is upward along the inclined plane, but gravity is downward along the inclined plane and larger. The resultant acceleration a2=-(5-3)=-2 m/s². The time for the block to decrease from 2 m/s to 0 is t2=2/2=1 s, and the displacement x2=2²/(2×2)=1 m. Therefore the highest position reached by the block is x1+x2=2+1=3 m. If it just cannot reach the top, then the minimum length of the conveyor belt inclined plane l0=3 m. Find the scratch length: At the highest point t=0.5+1=1.5 s, x=3 m, and afterward the block slides down from rest. When sliding down, it still slides downward relative to the conveyor belt, and the friction force is upward along the inclined plane, so the acceleration is still a=-2 m/s². From x=3 back to x=0, there is 0=3-(1/2)(2)τ²=3-τ², giving τ=√3 s. Use the belt material coordinate y=x-2t to represent the position of the belt material in contact with the block; ignoring the pulley size, the whole belt loop length is 2l0=6 m, so y is taken modulo 6 m. In the first and second stages, y increases from 0 to 1 m, and then returns to 0. In the sliding-down stage, let τ=t-1.5, then x=3-τ², y=x-2t=3-τ²-2(1.5+τ)=-τ²-2τ. When leaving the bottom end, τ=√3, and y=-(3+2√3), that is, in the sliding-down stage the material coordinate continuously decreases by 3+2√3 m, and this length is greater than 6 m. Since the contact material coordinate continuously sweeps over more than one complete belt loop, the entire belt is scratched, so the total scratch length s=2l0=6 m.
